name: Lockstep
description: An internal IT help desk: categories with sections nested inside them, each section its own page of answers, related questions under every answer, and a request form for whatever is not covered.
modelledOn: A company’s internal IT and workplace help desk
features: Preset: help centre — search hero, category tiles, popular questions
Nested sections: Accounts › Passwords, Devices › Laptops and phones
Each section is its own page: an accordion of its questions, the trail back, its sub-sections listed
Under every answer: related questions, the rest of its section, and “email me when this changes”
Pinned and badged questions; an Updated chip on anything changed this fortnight
Slate and teal, Inter, square corners
Zero custom CSS — every detail is a theme setting

collections.name: Accounts and access
collections.description: Signing in, passwords, two-step codes and who can see what.

pages.title: I am new — what do I need on day one?
pages.markdown: Your manager requests your accounts a week before you start. On day one, sign in with the temporary password in your welcome email, then set your own and enrol a two-step device.

pages.title: How do I get access to a shared drive or tool?
pages.markdown: Ask in the Access request form. The owner of the drive or tool approves it; most requests are done the same working day.

collections.name: Passwords and two-step
collections.description: Resets, lockouts and a new phone.

pages.title: How do I reset my password?
pages.markdown: Use “Forgot password” on the sign-in page. A reset link goes to your recovery email; it works for 30 minutes.

pages.title: I have a new phone — how do I move my two-step codes?
pages.markdown: Before you wipe the old phone, open Security settings and add the new device. If the old phone is gone, ask the help desk to reset two-step after a short identity check.

collections.name: Devices
collections.description: Laptops, phones, monitors and what to do when one breaks.

pages.title: My laptop is broken — what now?
pages.markdown: Save what you can to your drive and bring it to the IT desk. You get a loan laptop the same day while yours is repaired.

pages.title: Why does my laptop keep asking to restart?
pages.markdown: Security updates install overnight and need one restart. Restart before 6 pm and it will not ask again that day.

pages.title: Is my laptop encrypted?
pages.markdown: Yes. Every company laptop has full-disk encryption turned on before it reaches you; nothing for you to do.

collections.name: Phones
collections.description: Work phones and using your own.

pages.title: Can I read work email on my own phone?
pages.markdown: Yes, through the managed mail app. It keeps work data in its own space, which we can wipe without touching your photos or apps.

collections.name: Workplace
collections.description: Wi-Fi, printing, meeting rooms and visitors.

pages.title: How do visitors get on the Wi-Fi?
pages.markdown: Visitors join the Guest network and get a code from reception, valid for one day.

pages.title: How do I print?
pages.markdown: Send to “Office Printer” and release the job with your badge at any printer on any floor.
